A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DOT research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support matching retained, revised, and added content.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, cross-dataset evaluations, ablations, first-stage prediction experiments, and inference-time measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations across more datasets, model backbones, difficult inputs, and training-data sizes.

M1.justification: Equation 1 revises the stated view-ranking score from conditional generation probability to an entropy expression. The two-stage architecture, template selection framework, opinion exclusion, and training losses remain. The PDFs do not establish whether the revised equation reflects an implementation change.

E1.justification: Section 3.1 and Table 1 expand evaluation from five to nine datasets by adding MEMD Laptop, Books, Clothing, and Hotel. The original MEMD restaurant dataset, MR, is retained as M-Rest. The sentiment-quadruple extraction task remains unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds TAS-BERT, Extract-Classify, One-ASQP (large), SCRAP, and Qwen-2.5-7b. It reports GPT-4o instead of GPT-3.5-turbo and LLaMa-3.1-8b instead of LLaMa-3-8b, although Figure 9 retains older model labels. The principal generative baselines remain.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce T5-small and T5-large configurations, BART backbones, and quarter/half/full M-Rest training-data comparisons. Appendix G also defines a complex-input evaluation using more than three tuples, more than 22 words, or Flesch-Kincaid grade at least nine. These are additional evaluation protocols; the original training settings remain documented.

E4.justification: The ablation study adds stop-word-filtering and combined-component removals, while replacing the original no-resampling condition with random view sampling to test entropy-based selection. New analyses examine model scale, backbone dependence, implicit terms, training-data size, and complex sentences. The original case study and first-stage analysis are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions already report averaging over five seeds. v2 newly provides standard deviations for Paraphrase, MvP, and DOT on the five original benchmarks in Appendix G, Table 10. It does not report an increase in run count, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The original five DOT benchmark scores and cross-dataset results are unchanged, but v2 adds extensive benchmark and diagnostic results. SCRAP's newly included R16 score of 62.48 exceeds DOT's retained 61.24. The ablation Full Model entry changes from 53.94 to 54.33, and the no-multi-view entry from 53.31 to 52.31; these revisions do not establish reruns or a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: Equation 1 replaces a conditional-probability definition with a negative sum of probability-times-log-probability terms. This revises the mathematical definition of the ranking quantity. The training objectives and classification-loss derivation are retained, with no new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contribution: instance-specific DOT templates combine sentiment-extraction accuracy with faster inference and improved transferability relative to static prompting. Expanded benchmark evidence and updated dataset counts do not introduce a new central capability or novelty claim.

C2.justification: v2 changes the explanation for excluding opinions in stage one toward helping stage-two learning. It adds interpretations connecting implicit-term failures to data size, complex-sentence errors to fewer views, and seed variation to error propagation. It also explicitly limits the assumption that necessary views equal tuple count. Some interpretations overreach: the claimed superiority on BART and complex inputs has Rest-dataset exceptions in Tables 7 and 8.

D1.justification: v2 adds a reported public implementation link, literal-null handling, constrained-decoding disclosure, worked input/target examples in Appendix E, dataset statistics, and training durations. These materially expand reproducibility information without establishing newly introduced procedures. The original optimizer, learning rate, batch sizes, training epochs, and hardware remain; the Ethics Statement still describes release as planned.

R1.justification: v2 broadens citations and brief positioning to extraction-based and reasoning-based ABSA, newer LLMs, constrained decoding, BART, scaling laws, and readability analysis. The central relationship to static single-view and multi-view prompting remains unchanged. Consolidating the two Hu 2022 references does not represent a new cited work.

P1.justification: Section 2 is substantially rewritten to distinguish views, initial/final templates, and inference steps. The results narrative is reorganized around transferability, model scale, and ablations; the main-text case study moves to Appendix B, and the appendix structure expands substantially. These changes go beyond adding experimental paragraphs.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 are redrawn, and Table 1 becomes a full-width comparison with nine datasets, averages, and additional methods. v2 adds the model-scale chart, worked-example figure, and Tables 5–10. The original case-study, tuple-distribution, timing, and LLM-prompt displays are retained with relocation or renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of DOT's design through broader comparisons, explicit filtering and entropy-selection controls, backbone tests, and targeted failure analyses. Standard deviations, training costs, and clearer implementation documentation address important transparency gaps in v1. These gains concern evidential support rather than improved scores on retained benchmarks. Overgeneralized interpretations and inconsistent LLM labels remain weaknesses, but they do not outweigh the substantial improvement in experimental scrutiny and reproducibility information.
